title: Invited: Using Causal Information to Enable More Efficient Robot Operation
problem: How can robots learn to transfer and generalize causal models from limited human-generated examples to enable efficient operation on previously unknown tasks? Generating human-like causal models for unknown tasks by learning from small datasets of causal models on related tasks.
motivation: Causal reasoning enables humans to effortlessly transfer knowledge between different domains; enabling robots to perform similar transfers would allow them to generalize to new tasks with minimal human intervention.
method: The approach uses two strategies to transfer cause-and-effect understanding (called causal models—knowledge of what actions cause what outcomes) across objects. One-to-one transfer applies a learned causal model from one object directly to another similar object. Many-to-one transfer combines cause-and-effect patterns learned from multiple objects or users to understand an entirely new object. Researchers collected human-demonstrated causal models for light-producing objects, tested whether these patterns could transfer to new objects, and used the transferred understanding to guide robot tasks.
key_novelty: Robots can automatically transfer cause-and-effect understanding learned from human examples to unfamiliar objects and tasks, avoiding the need for experts to reprogram each new scenario.
contributions: Two transfer learning methods (one-to-one and many-to-one) for generalizing human causal models to new tasks
User study establishing human-generated causal models for light-producing objects
Framework demonstrating that causal models can guide downstream robot tasks including assembly, troubleshooting, and repair
Approach for replicating human-like causal reasoning in autonomous agents for unknown scenarios
primary_theme: Transfer learning via causal models for robot generalization
